messages.subject: Standard deviation and stacked barcharts
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have a small plotting challenge for the ggploters out there (I'll be
specific in presenting it because it is clearer):

I have replicated counts of some organisms, classified in size
fractions, at different depths. I want to plot a graph that would
represent simultaneously:
- the proportion of each size fraction
- the total amount at each depth
- the variance in the abundance of each of these categories and
possibly of the total

My initial guess was to use stacked barcharts to represent both the
relative abundance of each size fraction and the total amount. But I
can't find a legible way to put standard deviation for each size
fraction on such a graph. What would you do? Is there something that
takes care of that already in ggplot?


Code example:

# count data
datCounts = data.frame(depth=c(rep(10,10), rep(20,10)),
class=rep(c(rep("<3",5), rep(">3",5)),2), abund=c(runif(10),
runif(10)*2))
# the goal is to compare the profile of some governing parameter to
the abundances of the organisms, this is the profile
datProfile = data.frame(depth=0:30, value=(rnorm(31)))

# split the view
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(nrow=1, ncol=3)))

# plot the profile
p1 = ggplot(datProfile) + geom_path(aes(x=-depth, y=value)) +
coord_flip()
print(p1, vp=viewport(layout.pos.row=1, layout.pos.col=1))

# plot the abundances on the same scale
p2 = ggplot(datCounts) +
geom_bar(mapping=aes(x=-depth, weight=abund, fill=class),
binwidth=1) +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-30,0)) +
coord_flip()
print(p2, vp=viewport(layout.pos.row=1, layout.pos.col=2))
# the use of stacked bar charts gives information on both the total
abundance at each depth and the composition of the assemblage. In
addition, the bars are thin enough to situate them well in depth,
which is useful for the comparison with the profile. However the
abundances obviously vary in time and place, and what is represented
is currently just the sum.
# how could I plot the mean and add standard deviation to this kind of
plot?

# one possiblity would be to dodge bars instead of stacking them but
then the total abundance is not as obvious:
datSummary = ddply(datCounts, .(depth, class), function(x){
data.frame(mean=mean(x$abund), sd=sd(x$abund))
})
p3 = ggplot(datSummary, aes(x=-depth)) +
geom_bar(aes(y=mean, fill=class), binwidth=1, position="dodge",
stat="identity") +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-30,0)) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=(mean+sd),ymin=(mean-sd)), position="dodge",
width=2) +
coord_flip()
print(p3, vp=viewport(layout.pos.row=1, layout.pos.col=3))

# result: http://jo.irisson.free.fr/dropbox/bar_errorbar.png


# Additional remarks (which I am sure Hadley is well aware of, but
just in case...):

# 1/ bindiwdth does not work in the last construction of geom_bar,
with stat="identity". I agree it does not make much sense when there
is just one value but there should probably still be a way to control
the width of the bar.

# 2/ The way to add error bars to such a bar chart kind of looks like
a hack. Fortunately plyr makes it easy to compute the summary stats.
But the use of stat="identity" with just one value seems "hacky" and
the placement of the bars when width is specified (as emphasized here)
is sub-optimal. I would expect that to be just an option in most of
ggplot geoms, like errorbar=TRUE, or errorbar="sd"/"se"/"none"

# 3/ there seem to be a quirk in the placement of bars in geom_bar:
ggplot(datCounts) + geom_bar(aes(x=-depth, weight=abund, fill=class),
binwidth=4) + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-30,0)) + coord_flip()
# --> bars correctly centered on 10 and 20
ggplot(datCounts) + geom_bar(aes(x=-depth, weight=abund, fill=class),
binwidth=2) + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-30,0)) + coord_flip()
# --> bars _starting_ on 10 and 20, but not centered while they could
easily be since the binwidth is even.


Thanks in advance for you help.

Jean-Olivier Irisson
